The web just got a serious upgrade.  

htmx 4.0 lands with native Server‑Sent Events support, declarative WebSocket bindings, and a revamped “trigger” syntax that lets me fire actions on scroll, focus, or even CSS state changes—all without writing a single line of JavaScript. The new “swap‑once” mode also solves the long‑standing flicker problem when swapping large fragments, making progressive‑enhancement feel as snappy as a SPA.

What this means for me is a shift back to server‑driven UI logic. I can keep the heavy lifting in the backend, let htmx handle the DOM plumbing, and still get real‑time interactivity. It’s a reminder that the “write‑less‑JS” mantra isn’t a nostalgia trip—it’s a productivity win, especially for teams that already own robust APIs.

I’m already prototyping a dashboard that swaps charts on hover using only htmx attributes. If the same pattern scales, we could retire a chunk of client‑side codebases that are currently locked into React or Vue.

How will you rethink your next UI with htmx’s new capabilities?
